name: Ron-RonTheProducer
notes: The architect of "traffic music", and the best-sourced producer entry in this batch — the interview covers sound, drums, bass, synths, DAW and session workflow. His own framing is **"three different sounds of LA beats" blended in one**: Detroit-influenced trap, contemporary LA, and classic DPG-derived West Coast, which is why `relatedGenres` reaches `detroit-bounce` and `g-funk` rather than staying inside the lane. Two parameters are the record. (1) **"Thundering basslines"** — the loudest element, long and distorted, two-note riffs with audible portamento — so `bass808.distortion` is `heavy`, `slideProb` 0.5 with a 90ms portamento, and the `bassline` is an `independent_riff` at `followRootsProb` 0.70 with two-note `cellShapes`, because the research says the bass, not the synth, reads as the melody. (2) **"Laser synths"** — "bright saw/square leads with fast pitch envelopes and short decay, one voice only, over a static chord" — hence `articulation` `staccato`, `motifPitchCount` [2,4], `extensions.triad` 0.80 and `impliedByRiff` true. "16th hats that mute for whole verses" is `hihat.continuous` false; `fillDensity` stays at 0.30 because a model that declares a hat block still owes every seed a hat. ⚠ The research gives the 808 register as **E1–B1**, a 7-semitone window. `drums.bass808.register` is widened to [28,40] and `bassline.register` to [28,44] because a 7-semitone pool cannot produce a distinct bass part across seeds — this is an engine accommodation, not a reading of the records, and `followRootsProb` is kept high so the line stays rooted where the research puts it. ⚠ `medium` rather than high because the research marks him high-medium. The INFERRED parameters are the harmonic families (he is documented only as "static chord"; the `i–VII` and `i–VI` entries below are inference carrying the chord part's required variety) and the A♭/C major end of the key set, which is described but not measured. ⚠ The 140 BPM half-time population is documented and NOT modeled — one `halfTime` boolean, no modes authored. ⚠ DAW lineage is **FL Studio** and the session method is first-take (several beats played in succession, the artist raps over each immediately): that is `switchUpProb` 0.04 and loop-static, short forms. ⚠ **The countermelody reached only 976 distinct answers in 1000 seeds against a floor of 980**, so it was given range: densityRatio 0.45. A counter is combinatorial in the styles it may pick, its density against the melody, and the phrase length it answers inside — one style over a thin density inside a single phrase length has almost nothing a seed can vary. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [1,2], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count.
